abstract: Ionic liquids exhibit wide electrochemical windows, negligible volatility, and strong design flexibility, making them promising electrolytes for next-generation energy storage devices. However, the vast design space renders conventional trial-and-error discovery inefficient. Here, we develop a reinforcement learning framework for the de novo inverse design of potential dicyanamide-anion-based ionic liquids with enhanced Nernst-Einstein conductivity. A recurrent neural network trained on known cation structures was coupled with Monte Carlo tree search to generate novel cations. A forward predictive machine learning model was implemented as the reward function, guiding the search toward candidates with high Nernst-Einstein conductivity. Generated structures were subsequently evaluated using molecular dynamics simulations, and the resulting Nernst-Einstein conductivity data were iteratively incorporated to retrain and refine the forward model, forming a closed reinforcement learning loop. Through five iterations, the maximum molecular-dynamics-simulated Nernst-Einstein conductivity of the generated potential ionic liquids increased from 0.61 S/m to 3.77 S/m. The liquid-state character and the synthesizability of the generated candidates remain to be established. The proposed framework could facilitate the computational screening of ionic liquids with desired properties.
